name: GLEN Industries Limited
summary:
GLEN is a real, growing food-packaging manufacturer, but not yet a demonstrated high-quality cash compounder. The right current classification is an expansion and funding special situation under research hold, not a clean long-term compounding candidate. FY 23–FY 26 revenue CAGR 19.56% survives a materials-adjusted 19.00% value-added cross-check. Yet FY 26 operating EBITDA fell to 37.03 cr, PAT fell 9.44%, and reported CFO 5.8482 cr becomes negative 3.5059 cr after financing interest. Cash conversion, project funding and the rights of subsidiary preference capital matter more than the attractive sustainability narrative.

At the 19 October 2026 secondary BSE close 108.50, common market value is 261.07 cr on 24,061,370 shares. BQS 4.94; GQS raw 5.65 capped at 5.00 for persistent CASH 3; IAS is NS because R is not supportable from a verified funded ordinary base. These are provisional book-wide comparisons, not a recommendation or a personal allocation. Estimated L 7 applies only to the 5 lakh reference position and historical data.

The expansion base projects 470 cr FY 31 sales and 19% operating EBITDA margin, but even an optimistic 50 cr incremental project-loan availability assumption plus earmarked IPO deposits leaves a 49.46 cr peak cash gap. Hypothetical new equity at 86.80 per share increases common shares to 2.975930 cr and yields 14.88% five-year return, just below the common 15% nominal pre-investor-tax hurdle. That is a rescue sensitivity, not available financing. The bear rescue loses about 40% of per-share principal; the bull requires stronger margins, faster cash conversion and further funding. No positive return is attached to an unfunded ordinary case.

This is not a finding of inevitable failure. Existing operations with no discretionary expansion, stable working capital and normal revolving-credit continuity can meet known claims. Accordingly G 3 is Hold, not Fail. The September 15 court judgment quashed the 3.9128 cr DGGI notice/order; that is favorable evidence, not an expected tax bill. The separate 0.0808 cr West Bengal case and appeal finality remain open. Before any implementation, require the current debt/undrawn-facility bridge, remaining project invoices, project commissioning and first post-expansion operating cash evidence, plus Glen Realty preference terms.

GOV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
GOV.reason: Disclosed bank-return, charge and share-count inconsistencies and opaque subsidiary preference rights justify only middle-band stewardship, not an integrity failure. Family control and upward remuneration authorizations merit oversight.
GOV.contrary_evidence: Unmodified audit, clean reported audit trail, no reported default, explained peer-review-driven auditor replacement and favorable GST judgment weigh against alleging fraud or diversion.

MOAT.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
MOAT.reason: Real manufacturing know-how, customer qualification and recurring international relationships support a useful commercial position, but protected pricing, exclusive contracts and hard switching costs are not established. Polymer conversion remains competitive.
MOAT.contrary_evidence: Thin-wall revenue rose about 34% and utilization reached 77.74%. Broad distribution and internal tooling can aid service; larger qualified peers and weak straw utilization limit the moat case.

REV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
REV.reason: FY 23–FY 26 revenue CAGR 19.5606% maps to 7; materials-adjusted value-added CAGR 18.9991% supports the same band. The five-year 31.50% figure is shown but not scored because FY 21 is pandemic/start-up affected and FY 22 includes an acquired business. No trajectory bonus from preliminary H 1.
REV.contrary_evidence: FY 26 nominal sales outran physical tonnage and value added was flat year on year. Preliminary H 1 growth 18.84% nevertheless supports continuing demand rather than a collapsing revenue base.

DUR.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
DUR.reason: Accessible foodservice and QSR channels, international customers and planned container/paper-cup capacity create opportunities beyond a generic TAM. Existing reach and new products support a moderately attractive runway.
DUR.contrary_evidence: There are no firm take-or-pay contracts. Low straw utilization, construction delays and conditional funding limit monetizable runway. The 500 cr revenue target is guidance, not booked business.

CAP.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
CAP.reason: Three-year incremental normalized return about 12.47% is around the 12–15% analytical capital-cost range; latest average-capital ROIC about 10.48% trails it. CWIP, revaluation and acquired capital are not removed to manufacture attractive returns.
CAP.contrary_evidence: FY 25 operating profits and returns improved materially. Mature new-project utilization could improve economics, but FY 26 NOPAT fell while capital rose. Excluding only unrestricted cash lowers returns further.

CASH.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
CASH.reason: FY 24–FY 26 cumulative reported CFO/PAT is about 0.58 and after-finance cash is approximately zero. FY 25 and FY 26 after-interest CFO are negative. Inventory, receivables and vendor advances, not merely discretionary capex, explain weak realization. Persistent weakness triggers the GQS cap 5.
CASH.contrary_evidence: FY 23 and FY 24 generated positive after-interest CFO, and FY 26 receivables are reported under six months. Inventory normalization could release cash, but a future release is not cash already received.

BAL.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
BAL.reason: Gross debt is 3.26× operating EBITDA, with very little unrestricted cash and a large capex/working-capital requirement. EBIT/finance coverage 3.10× and current term maturity 8.6923 cr provide no large funding buffer.
BAL.contrary_evidence: IPO and preference capital strengthened book equity; debt fell 12.10 cr and no default was reported. Restrained operations can service known claims with normal rollovers, so G 3 Fail would overstate the evidence.

EXEC.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
EXEC.reason: Management built real scale and expanded container production, but project cost rose from 100.22 cr to 130–135 cr and commissioning slipped. Revenue growth alongside falling profit and mixed utilization supports average rather than premium execution.
EXEC.contrary_evidence: Actual domestic customer growth and manufacturing history are positive. Delays were attributed to building approvals, not an abandoned project; financial-control reconciliations still require closure.

EARN.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
EARN.reason: FY 23–FY 26 earnings expanded from a small, extraordinary-charge-affected base. FY 26 PAT 16.50 cr remains operating-profit driven, but fell 9.44%; operating margin compressed and current-share EPS 6.8585 is below FY 25 pro-forma EPS 10.375 on its then-existing share count; IPO dilution compounds the profit decline.
EARN.contrary_evidence: No exceptional profit is needed to explain FY 26 PAT. Other income 2.03 cr and weak cash conversion limit quality; subsidiary preference profit-participation rights remain unresolved.

R.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
R.reason: A reproducible whole-group bridge exists, but the ordinary expansion base is not funded even under the optimistic conditional 50 cr incremental draw. Actual undrawn capacity, invoices and recapitalization terms are not established. Positive rescue IRRs cannot be substituted for an ordinary return score.
R.contrary_evidence: Restrained survival is funded. The hypothetical base equity rescue resolves cash needs but yields 14.8788%, slightly below the common 15% hurdle. Unsupported rescue terms do not make that a scoreable ordinary base.

D.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
D.reason: The credible 15% margin and 15-extra-working-capital-day restrained stress requires 5.93 cr of liquidity. The expansion bear requires 79.78 cr hypothetical rescue and produces about 65.00 terminal value per diluted share. Funding and recapitalization expose common equity to material impairment.
D.contrary_evidence: Unstressed restrained operations survive after known tax, employee, statutory and capital claims. The quashed DGGI demand is not an expected payment; neither default nor inevitable insolvency is demonstrated.

P.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
P.reason: The common 15% hurdle at 8× terminal EBITDA and 120 cr net senior claims needs 424.41 cr revenue at 19% margin, with no new dilution. The base can reach that operating scale, but financing dilution reduces its return to 14.88%. Several operating and funding conditions must coincide.
P.contrary_evidence: The 15.82× headline PAT multiple is not extreme, and 8× terminal EBITDA is not a heroic converter multiple. Nevertheless the quote has no demonstrated cash/funding margin for error; the additional 18% hurdle needs 471.88 cr under the same simple reverse assumptions.

L.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.
L.reason: All 60 daily low/high×volume bounds imply 42.372–44.478 lakh conservative daily value and 2.248–2.360 sessions for 5 lakh at 5%, wholly within the 7–8 band. Use lower 7. A four-lot 5.208 lakh position needs four median daily whole-lot capacity units, also in that band.
L.contrary_evidence: Only 44/60 and 11/20 sessions permit at least one whole lot at 5%. At 2%, median capacity is zero. Live spread, depth and exact BSE restrictions remain unverified, so no executable exit schedule or upper-band score is claimed.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Research cutoff 20 October 2026; information obtained 21 October is restricted to documents and trades dated at or before cutoff. Valuation entry is 19 October 2026; five-investor-year endpoint 19 October 2031. Issuer: Glen Industries Limited, ISIN INE 0 UMC 01019, BSE 544444, symbol GLEN, BSE SME. The exchange interoperability master is used to verify the lot and shares, not to relabel GLEN as an NSE-listed company. Financial amounts are INR crore unless explicitly stated. Archetype: capital-intensive food-packaging converter, with polymer pass-through, export qualification, capacity utilization and inventory funding central to the economics.

G 1 Conditional: disclosed control weaknesses and concentrated stewardship need scrutiny, but reviewed evidence does not establish diversion or fraud. G 2 Conditional: audited core statements are usable with explicit reconciliations; residual preference, vendor-advance and bank-reporting gaps are important. G 3 Hold: new-facility funding is not fully demonstrable; restrained-operation survival prevents a forced failure verdict. G 4 Conditional: dated transactions, complete 60-session data and a 1200-share lot are established, but exact current BSE restriction circular and live depth are not.

High-confidence facts include audited FY 26 P&L, debt, cash-flow classification and parent common share count. Medium confidence applies to normalized capital returns, growth decomposition, customer advantage, the legal-text matching and secondary bounded liquidity. Low confidence applies to actual undrawn loan availability, current project cash-to-complete, preference rights, post-March unrestricted cash and a funded ordinary investor return. Forecast uncertainty is very high and different from source confidence. Ordinary return/IAS remain NS; supported historical factors are not erased because a separate funding question is unresolved.

March 2026 is the latest audited balance sheet used, not a verified October cash position. A secondary August monitoring summary says June IPO funds were 44.00 cr utilized and 12.59 cr remaining, which supports deployment continuing but cannot replace an audited full funding bridge. Preliminary H 1 sales are not audited H 1 earnings. No missing field is replaced with a neutral score, and no zero is substituted for an unknown liability, coupon, order book or available facility.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Factor scores and source confidence: GOV 5 Medium; MOAT 5 Medium; REV 7 Medium; DUR 6 Medium; CAP 4 Medium; CASH 3 High; BAL 4 Medium; EXEC 5 Medium; EARN 5 Medium; R NS Low; D 3 Medium; P 4 Medium; L 7 Medium. The attached factor audit supplies evidence and contrary evidence for every factor. None is 9–10; no exceptional-history ceiling is bypassed.

Exact Decimal BQS contributions are GOV 1.00 + MOAT 1.00 + REV 0.84 + DUR 0.60 + CAP 0.48 + CASH 0.30 + BAL 0.32 + EXEC 0.40 =4.94. No valuation or share-price penalty enters business quality.

GQS is Growth Quality Score, not governance: REV 2.80 + DUR 1.20 + EARN 0.75 + CAP 0.60 + CASH 0.30 =5.65 raw. Persistent poor realization through FY 24–FY 26, including negative after-interest cash in FY 25/FY 26, activates the CASH≤3 cap; final GQS 5.00. CAP 4 does not independently trigger the cap. A new expansion story does not excuse the repeated working-capital absorption.

IAS uses unrounded final BQS: quality 1.235 + unknown 0.35×R + downside 0.60 + price 0.40 + liquidity 0.70. Known contribution 2.935, coverage 65%, missing-factor mathematical range 3.285–6.435; final IAS NS. These endpoints are not probabilities or rankable investment scores. There is no reweighting and no invented R 5. R is missing because the credible expansion base requires unverified incremental financing and rescue terms, not merely because G 3 says Hold. The separate restrained business boundary is not silently substituted for the whole-company expected strategy.

BQS and GQS may enter provisional quality comparisons with their caveats. IAS is ineligible for an attractiveness ranking until a defensible funded ordinary base is established. G 1/G 3/G 4 failure overrides are not activated. Cross-company 0.1-point differences should not be treated as precision in economic truth.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company began as Glen Stationery in 2007 and moved into food packaging around 2019, after the 2018 name change. Its present business manufactures thin-wall food containers, PLA straws and paper straws, plus a small mould-design service stream. Products serve foodservice, QSR, FMCG and retail customers through domestic distribution and exports. The operating engine is the conversion of resin/paper inputs into qualified, customer-specific packaging, not a software-like recurring fee or a patented pharmaceutical franchise.

FY 26 category revenue was approximately 168.03 cr thin-wall containers,23.89 cr PLA straws,10.97 cr paper straws and 0.23 cr services. The container share is about 82.7%, so a three-product description does not mean equal diversification. Domestic product sales 147.5323 cr drove growth, whereas export products 55.3621 cr were below 56.1613 cr in FY 25. Services 0.2317 cr compare with 0.9793 cr. Statements of rising exports in introductory management commentary should therefore not displace the audited geographic revenue bridge.

As of FY 25/26, annual installed capacities were 7986 MT containers,1928 MT PLA straws and 1134 MT paper straws. FY 26 output 6209/525/387 MT implies container utilization 77.74%, PLA 27.23% arithmetically and paper 34.13%. Presentation/call PLA utilization 28.33% does not reconcile to the stated capacity/output; this is retained as a disclosure inconsistency rather than force-fitted. Planned incremental container capacity 13109 MT and paper-cup capacity 7696 MT are an expansion proposal, not existing fully utilized output.

Glen Realty and Glen Paper Product are subsidiaries with 99.98% ordinary-equity ownership disclosed. Glen Realty's FY 26 capital 8.15 cr includes the newly reflected 8.14 cr preference component; its turnover is zero and loss 0.1152 cr. The subsidiaries do not create a separate high-growth earnings story. Their assets, liabilities and preference claims are included in the group perimeter; intercompany investments are not added a second time to terminal value. Under the reported Indian Accounting Standards exemption, the statements follow applicable Accounting Standards rather than assuming Ind AS treatment.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest positive case is operational: food-contact quality, consistent moulding/printing, reliable delivery, customer-specific tools and export qualification can make an established supplier harder to replace than a commodity spot vendor. Management describes more than 40 recurring international customers and reach across 26 states and 30-plus countries. These facts support relationships and execution capability, but verified retention cohorts, share of wallet, exclusive tooling ownership, contractual pricing escalators and customer switching costs were not supplied.

The counter-case is substantial. The RHP says orders are not backed by firm long-term purchase commitments. Its top 10 domestic customer revenue 50.6527 cr plus top 10 export customer revenue 45.3346 cr totals 56.24% of group sales, but these are two separate customer sets and must not be mislabeled as top 10 overall concentration. Resin/paper inflation and mix can raise nominal revenue without increasing units or contribution. FY 26 container revenue rose about 33.9% against only 2.34% more reported container tonnage, while total category tonnage rose about 1.19%. That does not prove pricing power; mix, realizations and production-versus-sales timing need reconciliation.

Three economic peers provide context without pretending identical businesses. Rajshree Polypack makes food-grade sheets and thermoformed containers/cups; CRISIL reports FY 26 operating income 332.2 cr and notes fragmented competition and volatile polymer costs. Mold-Tek Packaging is much larger: FY 25 sales 781.32 cr, operating EBITDA 143.83 cr and volume 38264 MT, with IML/tooling capabilities and food/FMCG exposure. TPL Plastech manufactures industrial drums and IBCs, a less direct comparator that illustrates qualification and scale in another plastic-conversion niche. GLEN's full product, margin and cash profile is not interchangeable with any of them.

No same-date peer multiple set was independently assembled, so no invented sector median, target premium or relative discount supports the valuation. A narrow-to-moderate operational advantage is plausible, but durable high excess returns are not demonstrated. MOAT 5 is deliberately distinct from REV 7: selling more is not by itself evidence of a widening moat. Sustainability branding also does not eliminate regulation, resin exposure, customer bargaining or competing recyclable materials.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Audited/reconciled revenue history is FY 21 51.6560 cr, FY 22 93.8537 cr, FY 23 118.8507 cr, FY 24 144.5002 cr, FY 25 170.6608 cr and FY 26 203.1261 cr. Original FY 21/22 statements use₹000, converted by 10000 to crore; later statements use lakhs, converted by 100. FY 25 is the later annual comparative, not silently mixed with the slightly different RHP restatement.

The selected scoring window is FY 23–FY 26 before calculating the score. Its 19.5606% CAGR falls in the 15–20% REV 7 band. The five-year FY 21–FY 26 CAGR 31.5010% is disclosed but not used because FY 21 is pandemic/start-up affected and the FY 22 Ostern thin-wall-business transaction makes that baseline materially non-comparable. Choosing the mature three-year window reduces, rather than opportunistically raises, the rating. The underlying historical organic/acquisition separation is not precise enough to claim a clean five-year organic 9.

A converter must be tested on economic value added. Sales less materials consumed plus inventory build is 49.7523 cr in FY 23 and 83.8387 cr in FY 26:18.9991% three-year CAGR, independently supporting the same 7 band. This is a proxy, not formal gross profit, because direct expenses remain below it and inventory recognition can affect timing. FY 25 value added 84.4320 cr was slightly higher than FY 26 despite 19.02% revenue growth. Therefore the latest year's growth is not automatically better unit economics.

Growth sources are uneven. Containers grew rapidly in rupee terms while PLA revenue fell from 34.51 cr to 23.89 cr. Domestic products expanded from 113.5203 cr to 147.5323 cr; export products declined. Current capacities have some container headroom but large spare straw capacity, so new-site demand cannot be assumed merely from aggregate TAM. No defensible paid order-book total was found; none is fabricated.

The October 6 management H 1 FY 27 update gives sales 113.57 cr, +18.84%, container output 3133 MT and exports 26%. It supports continuing sales momentum but does not establish H 1 margin, profit or cash conversion. A mixed-source TTM revenue diagnostic is 221.1381 cr using audited FY 26 plus preliminary H 1 minus prior H 1; it is not audited TTM. One preliminary half-year is insufficient for a trajectory bonus, and revenue from uncommissioned capacity is not counted as delivered.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
There is a concrete reinvestment plan, not just an abstract packaging-market forecast. The RHP project cost 100.22 cr comprised land/site, building, electrical infrastructure and machinery, with 47.73 cr IPO allocation,50 cr planned bank borrowing and 2.49 cr already incurred internally. It separately disclosed 57.62 cr bank-sanctioned term loans. By May 2026 management described total project cost 130–135 cr, additional products/scope and imported-input/foreign-exchange effects, with the extra 30–32 cr supposedly funded internally. The economic question is whether that internal surplus exists after inventory, interest, taxes and debt service.

The five-year model does not answer that with an EBITDA headline. Sales growth requires operating working capital and maintenance capital as well as project investment. Even the base's declining working-capital intensity 52% to 48% of sales consumes cash as revenue rises 235→310→375→425→470 cr. Base margins 17→18→19→19→19% require recovery from FY 26 operating 18.23% without assuming FY 25's 23.64% persists. Project cash 110 cr is an explicit unverified remaining-cost assumption within a 95–120 cr range, not an audited unpaid invoice balance. Already-paid capital advances are not added again; a linked vendor-advance reclassification lowers both opening operating assets and remaining project cash by 12.085 cr, leaving the funding result unchanged.

Full-capital returns are ordinary, not exceptional. Book equity including preference plus debt less cash/bank gives invested-capital proxies 114.1087 cr in FY 23,132.9057 cr FY 24,189.2239 cr FY 25 and 226.5378 cr FY 26. At 25% normalized tax, NOPAT rises 7.7657→13.6298→24.7348→21.7836 cr. FY 26 return on average capital is about 10.48%; FY 23–FY 26 incremental NOPAT divided by incremental capital is about 12.47%, around the 12–15% analytical WACC range. These are analytical proxies, not management ROCE. Including restricted IPO cash in the deduction is favorable; excluding only unrestricted cash produces still lower returns. Revaluation reserve 12.0406 cr and acquisition capital reserve 6.0155 cr are not imaginary free cash or removable capital simply because they dilute ratios.

Cash quality is the binding constraint. FY 24–FY 26 cumulative reported CFO is 25.1656 cr against 43.3045 cr PAT, about 0.58×; subtracting financing interest leaves approximately negative 0.6083 cr. The GQS cap 5 therefore reflects repeated cash realization, not just a temporary capex year. A successful commissioning can improve CAP and EARN, but GQS should not be upgraded until receivables/inventory/advances convert to cash without new leverage. Faster sales alone could worsen the funding deficit.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Lalit Agrawal chairs the company; Nikhil Agrawal is managing director and his son; Niyati Seksaria is a whole-time director and Nikhil's sister. Family control can align long-term ownership, but minority investors depend on related-party, remuneration and capital-allocation discipline. The March 2026 shareholding file contains inconsistent totals: its share-count column 23,958,170 differs from voting-rights 24,061,370; promoter totals/percentages likewise differ. The audited parent capital and dated exchange security master establish 24,061,370 common shares. September promoter ownership 74.30% appears in secondary data but was not independently established from the exact latest primary filing; it is not substituted into a high-confidence ownership claim. March pledge/encumbrance and convertible/option columns do not show such instruments.

Auditor change needs its actual explanation. The annual report says joint auditor S.N. Guha resigned because the peer-review certificate was not renewed; Tosniwal & Associates filled the vacancy and was proposed for a five-year appointment. That is not evidence of an accounting-disagreement resignation. The reviewed opinion is unmodified, the FY 26 audit-trail reporting says the feature operated without reported tampering, and CARO reports no loan/interest default. CFO/company-secretary remuneration percentage increases partly reflect their September 2024 appointments, so full-year versus partial-year comparisons must not be called unexplained windfalls. Director remuneration revisions remain a monitoring item, not an allegation.

There are real disclosure/control concerns. Bank stock/current-asset returns differ from books, including a Q 4 stock difference 11.6837 cr; management attributes this to provisional operational estimates versus final counts/audit and debtor-receipt timing. Charge-registration/reconciliation issues are disclosed, with management referring to bank confirmations and intended corrections. These responses belong alongside the discrepancy, but do not prove it has been cured. The annual CSR shortfall 0.22 cr was intended to be spent by 30 September 2026; completion was not verified. The summary note saying there are no micro/small-enterprise dues sits awkwardly beside a 3.2061 cr MSME creditor category and requires reconciliation; it is not proof of undisclosed default.

Related-party funding includes 11.2436 cr long-term loans. That liability is not mislabeled as money diverted out of the company. Group intercompany items are eliminated; operating vendor advances 12.085 cr still need beneficiary, age and project/operating classification. The new preference 8.14 cr is reconciled to Glen Realty, not a parent common-capital overissue. Its holder, coupon, redemption, security, convertibility and economic participation remain unresolved; old parent preference coupons redeemed in 2024 cannot be transplanted to this instrument.

GST: the RHP/annual report matches demand 3.9128 cr, DGGI/KZU/24/093 dated 9 January 2024, to WPA 3254/2025. The September 15 judgment text quashes that notice and consequential 30 January 2025 order, discussing the omitted Rule 96(10). The company's earlier response was that the matter was revenue-neutral; the authority defended action under the law then applicable. The favorable result is included, but original court-copy and appeal finality are unverified. Separate 0.0808 cr WB demand/WPA 13552/2024 had a stay disclosed through 30 September 2026 only. No later outcome is invented and the quashed principal demand is not an ordinary cash expense.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Core earnings bridge: FY 26 revenue 203.1261 cr + other income 2.0325 cr − operating costs − depreciation 7.9901 cr − finance 9.3541 cr =PBT 21.7232 cr; current/deferred tax 4.6091/0.6116 cr gives PAT 16.5025 cr. Operating EBIT 29.0448 cr and EBITDA 37.0349 cr exclude other income. Company-presented EBITDA 38.5039 cr uses a narrower interest-cost addback; the all-finance-cost, other-income-included variant is 39.0674 cr. Those definitions are not interchanged to imply margin growth. FY 25 comparable operating EBITDA 40.3439 cr fell to 37.0349 cr; margin 23.64% fell to 18.23%.

Reported cash-flow classification is critical. Financing interest 9.3541 cr is outside CFO, so 5.8482 cr reported CFO is not post-interest owner cash. FY 26 after-interest CFO is−3.5059 cr and after-interest cash capex residual−23.8537 cr before other investing/financing flows. FY 25 equivalents are−3.2794 cr and−38.5938 cr. FY 23/FY 24 after-interest CFO 5.1486/6.1770 cr provide favorable contrary evidence but do not cancel subsequent deterioration. The original FY 22 cash-flow acquisition presentation includes a positive 6.01546 cr business-purchase line matching capital reserve, and acquisition working capital complicates normalization; long-window original cash numbers are disclosed without treating them as a clean organic series.

FY 26 pre-working-capital operating cash 37.6224 cr was absorbed by inventory 18.8252 cr, receivables 6.8340 cr and loans/advances 9.2670 cr. Higher trade payables 7.3967 cr and other movements partly offset it; tax paid 6.0185 cr left 5.8482 cr. Inventory 78.4152 cr is 38.60% of annual sales versus 34.92% FY 25. Receivables 37.1727 cr represent about 66.8 sales-days, versus 65.7 previously, and are classified as under six months/good. Stock composition is raw materials 33.0259 cr, WIP 18.0610 cr, finished goods 23.7100 cr and stores 3.6183 cr. No obsolescence haircut is asserted as fact, but inventory quality and realizable pricing require monitoring.

Balance-sheet cash is not all free. Cash/bank 33.8007 cr consists of 0.5177 cr cash equivalents and 33.2830 cr other deposits, including 32.1947 cr unutilized IPO deposits; another 0.9965 cr FD sits in noncurrent assets. The remaining 2.0848 cr collateral/deposit balance is unavailable for ordinary cash needs and only offsets terminal debt in a conditional solvent valuation. FD receipts rather than direct bank confirmation supported the auditor's verification: a limitation, not proof the funds are absent. IPO gross proceeds 62.9422 cr and new preference cash 8.14 cr are already received in the historical cash bridge, not new model funding.

Debt 120.7281 cr comprises 22.6784 cr long-term and 98.0497 cr short-term. Short-term includes cash credit 53.6768 cr, OD/EPC 24.9471 cr, buyer credit 9.1720 cr, other 1.5615 cr and current term maturities 8.6923 cr. Long-term includes bank term 8.4786 cr, finance lease 0.5255 cr, vehicle 0.5307 cr, related parties 11.2436 cr and other 1.90 cr. Gross debt/operating EBITDA 3.26×, EBIT/finance 3.10× and all-cash net debt/EBITDA 2.35× understate the practical funding pressure if restricted IPO cash cannot pay ordinary bills. Excluding only free cash yields 3.25×. No reported default is established.

Opening-claims settlement is explicit in the model. Inventory, receivables, operational advances and ordinary other assets less trade creditors 13.4236 cr, customer advances 0.4817 cr, expense liabilities 5.3813 cr and lease equalization 0.0237 cr produce operating working capital 110.2404 cr. Net current tax 3.3402 cr, statutory dues 0.4835 cr, CSR 0.22 cr, current employee provisions 0.0529 cr and capital creditor 0.1056 cr total 4.2022 cr, paid once in year 1 outside working capital. Tax is already net of advance tax/TDS; the extra disclosed TDS asset 0.0326 cr is conservatively not credited again. Capital advances 2.8917 cr are excluded from operating working capital and assumed already paid in the remaining-project-cost convention. The 0.2299 cr signed capital commitment is retained even in restrained operations and included within larger project budgets, not added twice.

Long-term employee provisions 0.6311 cr, customer security deposits 1.3239 cr, old deferred tax 4.9648 cr and a 0.005 cr ordinary-minority bound remain nominal terminal claims rather than arbitrary immediate cash bills. Preference 8.14 cr is a separate terminal senior-claim boundary in ordinary sensitivities, moved to cash only in a labeled early-redemption stress. No unknown coupon is invented. The subsidy receivable 2.923 cr and unused IPO balance under a paused project are not freely distributable common-equity addbacks. Debt includes lease principal; operating margins include ordinary rent, with no second invented lease liability. The severe GST reversal scenario is not an ordinary expected expense.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Dated entry 108.50 ×2.406137 cr common shares =261.0659 cr market capitalization. FY 26 PAT 16.5025 cr implies 15.82× earnings and current-share EPS 6.8585. Headline EV using all cash/bank is 347.9933 cr, about 9.40× operating EBITDA; adding preference 8.14 cr gives 356.1333 cr/9.62× before other senior claims. If only 0.5177 cr unrestricted cash is offset, common EV 381.2763 cr/10.29× and preference-adjusted 389.4163 cr/10.51×. The cash definition matters more than a cosmetic single EV multiple. No current price is represented as executable and no dividend is assumed in forecasts.

The model starts from the 31 March 2026 audited balance sheet, forecasts FY 27–FY 31 and adds a 202-day no-growth cash stub to 19 October 2031, exactly five investor years from entry. Terminal EV uses FY 31 annual operating EBITDA, excluding other income, at 6×/8×/10× in bear/base/bull; it is not the short stub's EBITDA multiplied by an annual multiple. The common benchmark is 15% nominal annual return before investor taxes;18% is a separate risk sensitivity, not the book's scoring hurdle. Future company cash taxes are 25% on positive earnings after modeled depreciation and interest. Maintenance spend and working capital are funded before equity value.

Ordinary bear/base/bull assumptions, all explicit rather than forecasts with probabilities:
- Bear sales 215/250/290/320/345 cr; margins 14.5/15/15.5/16/16%; working capital 57→53% of sales; remaining project cash 120 cr; maintenance 6→10 cr;6× terminal multiple.
- Base sales 235/310/375/425/470 cr; margins 17/18/19/19/19%; working capital 52→48%; project 110 cr; maintenance 6→10 cr;8× multiple.
- Bull sales 255/370/470/540/600 cr; margins 19/21/22/22/22%; working capital 48→42%; project 95 cr; maintenance 6→14 cr;10× multiple.
The FY 26 current term maturity 8.6923 cr is scheduled first. Amortization of the remaining 9.5348 cr old secured-term balance over the next three years and of a hypothetical new 50 cr term loan beginning FY 29 is a scenario, not a verified bank repayment contract. Revolving facilities and related-party loans are not all called at once. The long-grace sensitivity removes unverified later amortization; the base still needs 42.42 cr additional cash. Maintenance 4–8 cr and finance-cost continuity are tested separately for essential survival rather than forcing a large arbitrary cash buffer.

The sanctioned 57.62 cr RHP figure is not automatically undrawn. The ordinary growth sensitivities show zero,50 cr and 57.62 cr conditional incremental availability; the upper bounds may overstate genuinely available capacity if portions are already in opening debt or cash/project advances. No approval, covenant satisfaction or disbursement is assumed verified. Already received IPO cash is used only for authorized project spend, never added again as financing or used for unrelated claims. A secondary June monitoring balance 12.59 cr is not added to the March 32.1947 cr.

Even with 50 cr conditional new draws, peak deficits are bear 79.78 cr, base 49.46 cr and bull 20.24 cr. Their ordinary terminal equity prices/IRRs are null. With no incremental project draw, base gap 90.87 cr; with the full 57.62 cr conditional upper bound,43.16 cr. This is a funding diagnostic, not an assertion that the company has defaulted or cannot arrange finance.

Separately labeled equity rescue uses issue price 86.80,20% below the dated quote, zero assumed issue fees and enough cash exactly when a deficit occurs. It is not a financing commitment. Bear raises 79.78 cr, ends with 3.325310 cr shares and terminal common equity 216.15 cr, or 65.00/share and−9.74% annual return. Base raises 49.46 cr, ends with 2.975930 cr shares,122.50 cr debt and 67.09 cr cash; terminal common equity 646.01 cr is 217.08/share and 14.88% annual return. Bull raises 20.24 cr, ends with 2.639281 cr shares and terminal common equity 1326.85 cr, or 502.73/share and 35.89%. The corresponding existing-holder ownership reductions are 27.64%,19.15% and 8.83%. Debt-rescue base instead assumes additional 12% borrowing with joint interest/tax solving:56.78 cr required,239.47 terminal price and 17.16% return, but greater creditor risk and no verified lending offer. Neither rescue supplies R.

Reverse valuation, without assuming rescue dilution, at 8× terminal EBITDA and 120 cr net senior claims requires 424.41 cr sales at 19% margin for the 15% hurdle, equivalent to 15.88% five-year revenue CAGR. The 18% hurdle needs 471.88 cr/18.36% CAGR. Merely preserving nominal entry capital needs 250.70 cr sales under those same end-state assumptions. All are arithmetic requirements, not probabilities; actual financed claims and dilution can raise them. The matrix spans 6–10× multiples and 80–160 cr net claims. A ±2× terminal multiple shifts base rescue equity value by 178.6 cr before per-share effects. Margin, working-capital and financing misses are not repaired by assigning a higher multiple.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The credible loss mechanism is not simply a share-price wobble. Polymer/input inflation or weaker product mix compresses margins; inventory and customer advances tie up cash; the new facility takes longer to commission; lenders will not supply the assumed incremental line or request tighter terms; outside capital is raised at a discounted price. Existing shareholders then own a smaller share of an enterprise with more senior claims. A business can survive while the original investor permanently loses capital.

The restrained essential-operation test intentionally removes discretionary growth capex and new loans. Revenue stays 203.1261 cr, operating EBITDA 37.0349 cr, operating working capital remains 110.2404 cr, yearly maintenance 6 cr and the 0.2299 cr committed capital spend are retained. It pays 4.2022 cr old cash claims and the known 8.6923 cr first-year maturity, assumes continuity of ordinary revolving credit, and retains old deferred tax, employee, customer-deposit and preference claims at the endpoint. Year 1 closing free cash 4.15 cr is positive. Across maintenance 4–8 cr, first-year headroom remains positive. This is why a blanket G 3 Fail or immediate insolvency statement would be unjustified. Unused restricted IPO cash is not used to make this test pass.

A linked restrained stress is still uncomfortable: sales 193 cr,15% margin,15 extra sales-days of operating working capital and 9.5% old-debt interest give a 5.93 cr first-year funding gap. The stress does not call every bank loan, require all preference redemption or stack the large quashed GST demand. Normalized future operations can eventually produce cash, but cash later does not fund bills earlier. This remains a hypothetical liquidity need, not proof of present arrears. Actual cash since March and genuine undrawn limits determine whether it is bridgeable.

Additional independent claim sensitivities are separated. Paying preference face 8.14 cr immediately, if future evidence required it, turns the restrained case into a 3.99 cr gap; no such immediate legal obligation or coupon has been established. A 3.9936 cr combined GST cash payment is only a reversal/adverse-outcome boundary, not expected loss: the substantial DGGI case was quashed before cutoff, and even that separate sensitivity remains funded in the unstressed restrained case. Requiring a new draw to be zero materially worsens expansion funding but does not prove revolving-credit withdrawal.

A rough asset recovery cross-check is not a liquidation appraisal: applying 50–70% to group PPE/CWIP/intangibles,50–80% to inventory and 80–95% to receivables, while treating allcash/deposits at book subject to restrictions and advances at 0–50%, gives illustrative common recovery of 4.63–67.81 cr, or 1.92–28.18 per current share, after 159.31 cr senior and other claims. This corresponds to roughly 74–98% loss against entry, before liquidation costs. Cash realization at book is favorable and full deferred-tax face retention is conservative; these are boundaries, not expected outcomes. Specialized plant, stock mix, pledged assets and tax/employee priority prevent treating book equity 131.47 cr excluding preference as a cash floor. The model does not add PPE or working capital again on top of EBITDA enterprise value. D 3 reflects credible material impairment and adverse recapitalization, while favorable survival evidence rules out asserting certain total loss.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A 5× five-year common-share outcome requires 37.97% annual return;10× requires 58.49%. At unchanged 24,061,370 common shares and entry 108.50, those mean terminal prices 542.50/1085.00 and common market values 1305.33/2610.66 cr, before any rescue dilution. This is an investor outcome test, not a sales-growth slogan.

At 8× terminal operating EBITDA and 120 cr net senior claims,5× requires EBITDA 178.17 cr and revenue 937.72 cr at 19% margin, a 35.79% five-year revenue CAGR.10× requires EBITDA 341.33 cr and revenue 1796.49 cr, a 54.64% CAGR. At 10× EBITDA the necessary operating performance is lower, but that relies on a more generous retained multiple rather than just execution. The supplied reverse matrix spans 6/8/10× and 80/120/160 cr net claims so debt is not silently fixed at zero.

The announced manufacturing expansion and management's 450–500 cr scale ambition do not by themselves support 937–1796 cr revenue at high cash margins. Meeting 5× would likely require another phase of funded capacity, stronger utilization, more working capital, additional customers and substantially better cash conversion. Such spending cannot be assumed free or absent from share count. The linked bull, already requiring 600 cr revenue,22% margin,42% operating-working-capital intensity,10× terminal EBITDA and 20.24 cr equity rescue, reaches 502.73/share, about 4.63×, not 5×. Its 35.89% return is a conditional upside, not a base or probability-weighted fair value.

Neither 5× nor 10× qualifies as a supported ordinary five-year pathway today.5× is an aggressive conditional possibility only if operations, funding and terminal valuation cooperate beyond demonstrated evidence;10× is speculative rather than underwritten. The useful milestone is not a higher target price but whether new capacity produces cash and excess returns per existing share after all creditor and preference claims.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Current financing bridge, before reconsidering IAS: obtain lender-by-lender sanctioned, drawn and genuinely undrawn balances, validity, collateral, covenants, interest and repayment schedule. Reconcile to March debt 120.7281 cr and later receipts. Release the funding hold only if committed accessible sources cover remaining project cash, maintenance, working capital and all opening claims without an unspecified rescue.
2. Project completion and cash-to-complete, next substantive filing: reconcile revised 130–135 cr budget with invoices paid, vendor/capital advances, CWIP, approved orders and creditor balances. Confirm commercial commissioning and saleable output rather than a construction-progress statement. A further material cost rise or date slip weakens EXEC and the base.
3. First post-expansion cash result: monitor after-interest CFO, inventory/receivable days, the 12.085 cr vendor advances and customer deposits. Two successive periods of rising sales but negative after-interest CFO, or operating working capital above the base 52→48% trajectory, support retaining CASH 3 and GQS cap 5.
4. Preference instrument: obtain Glen Realty's FY 26 separate statements and instrument terms, holder, coupon/dividend participation, redemption/convertibility and any guarantees. Reflect verified claims rather than the model's no-invented-coupon and face-value terminal boundary.
5. Governance remediation: reconcile bank stock/receivable returns and registered charges, explain the shareholding-column mismatch, verify CSR 0.22 cr settlement and distinguish promoter purchases from business acquisitions. Unmodified audit alone does not close each item.
6. GST: verify the original September 15 judgment and any later stay/appeal, plus separate WPA 13552/2024 after September 30. Do not restore the quashed DGGI claim as ordinary liability merely because an older annual report listed it.
7. Execution economics: publish container/PLA/paper volumes, realizations and utilization consistently; reconcile 525 MT PLA with utilization and capacity. Watch margins, domestic/export mix and customer concentration alongside new-site output.
8. Before any trade: refresh actual BSE segment/surveillance, lot, spread and executable depth. For the 5 lakh reference, one lot costs 1.302 lakh; three lots are 3.906 lakh and four 5.208 lakh. Recalculate liquidity for the actual proposed position and accept that participation limits can imply no permissible whole-lot trade on many days.

These are research triggers, not scheduled monitoring commitments or instructions to a broker. No position, order, filing request or company contact has been initiated.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: conditional expansion/funding special situation; average-to-below-average demonstrated business quality, capped growth quality and incomplete investment attractiveness. It is not an established high-quality compounder, not a proven fraud, and not demonstrated insolvent. The favorable tax judgment and real sales growth must remain visible alongside cash and funding concerns.

Research action: retain on a funding-and-cash-conversion watchlist, with no score-derived buy conclusion. BQS 4.94 and GQS 5.00 are provisional quality scores; IAS NS is excluded from the attractiveness rank. No target purchase price can repair an unknown financing path on its own. An operating base can become scoreable only after the accessible facility/cash-to-complete/preference bridge is established; then recompute diluted equity return at the common 15% hurdle and the actual entry price.

What would improve the case: verified available project credit rather than a historical total sanction; commissioning within a reconciled cost envelope; meaningful sales from new capacity; operating working-capital intensity falling without overdue supplier dependence; repeated positive after-interest CFO; and clear subsidiary preference rights. Those would improve CAP/CASH/BAL and potentially R. What would weaken it: another unfinanced capex revision, continued inventory/advance growth, delayed collections, adverse bank covenant changes, a discounted recapitalization beyond modeled bounds or an adverse change to the legal position.

The market test is conditional too. Complete 60-session low/high×volume bounds support estimated L 7, not an executable 2.3-day exit promise. A four-lot position needs four median whole-lot daily-capacity units at 5%, and 16 of 60 observed sessions did not permit even one lot at that participation rate. At the 19 October 7200-share volume, a 1200-share lot alone is 16.67% of trading. Concentrated control, lot constraints and circuits can defeat an otherwise reasonable historical-capacity estimate. Any eventual implementation needs live verification and a position-specific test.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence controls the financial record: official issuer-linked FY 26 annual report and May results, RHP, FY 22 original statements, investor presentation, call transcript, March shareholding and the dated exchange interoperability master. Annual PDFs for FY 23–FY 25 are retained as background; relevant FY 23/FY 24 values are taken from the restated RHP and FY 25 from the later FY 26 annual comparative. Scanned FY 26 pages were inspected through image/OCR; source locators state physical versus printed pages. Secondary sources support the current historical quote, complete OHLCV window, preliminary H 1 update and legal transcript, with limitations stated.

No failed BSE document route was treated as proof that the filing did not exist. Exact H 1/monitoring documents and original court-copy access were not fully recovered; the unverified summary is labeled and does not become a model cash balance. The monitoring-summary figures reconcile directionally with deployment but not lender draws. Peer evidence is economic context with explicit dated periods; no fabricated current market multiple table is used.

Model assumptions are separate from facts: forecast revenue, margin, operating-working-capital ratios, maintenance,95–120 cr remaining project spend,0/50/57.62 cr incremental-credit bounds, future amortization after known current maturity,25% new-profit cash tax, no dividends,6–10× terminal operating EBITDA, collateral FD release/offset on solvent exit, preference face-value boundary and discounted equity/debt rescue. The March-to-October opening-balance staleness is a limitation. The model does not claim to know current bank cash, a coupon, a lender commitment, an executable equity issue price or the ultimate legal finality.

The 15% common hurdle is used for comparability;18% is an additional sensitivity only. The terminal date aligns to five investor years with a no-growth 202-day stub, not an accidental 4.45-year fiscal horizon. Negative cash at any intermediate point makes the ordinary path unfunded even if later cash recovers; no ordinary price/IRR is issued for it. Rescue cases explicitly add shares or interest-bearing debt and remain unverified conditions. No arbitrary cash reserve, immediate recall of all debt, or expected payment of the quashed GST claim is used to manufacture failure.

Open questions with the greatest decision value: current genuinely undrawn project facilities; invoices and legally committed cash-to-complete; operating versus project use/beneficiaries of vendor advances; Glen Realty preference terms and available group cash; updated statutory/CSR settlements; bank-return/charge reconciliation; original judgment/appeal and separate WB case status; primary latest ownership and exact BSE restrictions. Missing answers are not filled with zeros or neutral scores. The source ledger, verified-input file, opening-claims ledger, full model code/results,60-session raw data and QA make the analysis reproducible. All output remains private pending the parent task's review/publication decision.
